prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 会议室预订周视图（5/12–5/16） (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "2025 春季校园招聘宣讲会（09:00–17:" spans 3 col × 1 row; "产品需求评审（09:00–12:00）｜A301" spans 1 col × 2 row; "新员工入职培训（13:30–16:30）｜C20" spans 1 col × 2 row; "客户方案演示与答疑（13:30–16:30）｜A" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "时间段" · longest unbreakable word 53px · one-line width 94px
  col 2: header "周一（5/12）" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 261px
  col 3: header "周二（5/13）" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 214px
  col 4: header "周三（5/14）" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 274px
  col 5: header "周四（5/15）" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 304px
  col 6: header "周五（5/16）" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 190px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 682px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 681px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 682px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A weekly room-booking grid: a reader either (a) runs down one weekday column to find a free slot, or (b) reads across one time band to compare which day/room is free — it is a lookup-and-compare table, not a reading table, so the time axis and the day columns must be scannable at a glance rather than prose-legible.","reading":"Top-left time label → down the column for the target day, or across the row for the target slot. Merged blocks (Mon 产品需求评审, Wed 新员工入职培训, Thu 客户方案演示 spanning 09:00–10:30+10:30–12:00 / 13:30–15:00+15:00–16:30, and the 3-column 全天 banner over Wed–Fri) tell the reader 'this room/day is taken for a longer stretch', so they must stay visually unbroken and clearly wider than a single cell.","groups":["Col 1 (时间段) stands alone: it is the axis every other column is read against, so its widths are set by the time token, not by content length.","Cols 2–6 (周一–周五) are one family of identical role and identical header level; they should be within a few px of each other unless a column's content genuinely demands otherwise, because uneven day widths make horizontal comparison of free slots misleading.","Cols 4–6 (周三/周四/周五) are additionally bound together by the single 全天 banner that spans all three; their combined width is what that one long string has to live in, so they should not be squeezed simultaneously."],"keep_intact":["Time ranges 09:00–10:30, 10:30–12:00, 13:30–15:00, 15:00–16:30, 16:30–18:00 (never split mid-token)","Room codes A301, B202, B105, A301, C20 and 线上","Weekday headers 周一（5/12）… 周五（5/16） on one line","The ｜ separator between event name and room, and the parenthesised times inside event names (keep with their event)","The 3-column banner cell as one unbroken block across 周三–周五"],"may_wrap":["Event titles: 产品需求评审（09:00–12:00）, 供应商准入评审, 研发周会（15:00–16:00）, 周例会（09:30–10:15）, 合同条款会签, 法务咨询, 项目风险同步, 数据看板…, 算法模型…, 新员工入职培训（13:30–16:30）, 客户方案演示与答疑（13:30–16:30）, 产品灰度… — these wrap to 2–3 lines without loss of meaning","The 全天 banner string 2025 春季校园招聘宣讲会（09:00–17:00）｜报告厅 — it has the whole 全天 row to itself, so 2 lines there are free","Wrapping inside the two-row merged blocks (Mon 09:00–12:00, Wed/Thu 13:30–16:30) costs nothing in row height, since those rows are already double height"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[95,123,101,129,144,89],"idea":"Proportional to each column's longest single-line content, so 周四 and 周三 (the densest, with tall merged blocks) get the most room and 周五 the least, while 时间段 stays at its minimum one-line width."},{"name":"B","widths":[94,118,117,118,117,117],"idea":"Calendar rhythm: the time axis is pinned at exactly the 94px needed to keep 09:00–10:30 on one line, and the five weekdays are made effectively equal so a reader can compare the same time band across days without re-anchoring; all inequality is absorbed by 2–3 line wrapping, not by width."},{"name":"C","widths":[115,100,96,130,140,100],"idea":"Time-anchored with density tiers: a generous 115px time column (full time range plus air) makes the row axis the dominant reading path, 周三/周四 are widened because their two-row merged blocks and long titles need it, and the lighter 周一/周二/周五 are narrowed to pay for it."}]}
